A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Birch SGD framework. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices are readable and support comparison, including matching material moved or renumbered in v3.

before.justification: v1 reports original optimization experiments using simulated distributed environments: MNIST logistic regression, CIFAR10 with ResNet18, and Wikitext-2 with GPT2 (Appendix C).

after.justification: v3 retains those experiments and adds MNIST experiments investigating Cycle SGD under synchronization-dependent communication costs and Rennala SGD batch-size sensitivity (C.5–C.6).

M1.justification: The Birch SGD construction and proposed algorithms in Appendix E retain their procedures. Ringmaster's delay threshold is renamed from B to G without changing its update rule. Algorithm 20 newly documents canonical FedAvg for theoretical comparison; it is not a new proposed component.

E1.justification: The datasets and learning tasks remain MNIST, CIFAR10, and Wikitext-2. C.5 adds a distinct MNIST computing scenario where communication takes 1.5 times the number of synchronized workers in seconds, extending the earlier fixed and worker-dependent communication environments.

E2.justification: The existing experimental comparison methods are retained. New Figure 13 evaluates the already-proposed Cycle SGD against the existing set: Local SGD, Async-Local SGD, Rennala SGD, Ringmaster ASGD, and Synchronized SGD. Canonical FedAvg is added as an analytical comparison in Appendix H, without empirical results.

E3.justification: Existing settings and parameter grids in Tables 2–6 are unchanged. New C.5 uses 64 workers, computation time 10, synchronization-dependent communication, and Cycle groups of eight. C.6 uses 100 workers with computation/communication times 10/100 and B values 128, 256, 512, and 1024; its plotted learning rates are not all identical.

E4.justification: v3 adds two focused analyses absent from v1: C.5 tests whether Cycle SGD's reduced simultaneous synchronization benefits convergence under bandwidth pressure, and C.6 tests sensitivity to Rennala SGD's batch-size/tree-distance parameter. The earlier analyses remain.

E5.justification: Both versions report selected grid-search convergence curves without repeated-seed counts, confidence intervals, or statistical significance tests. The additional experiments do not introduce uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Existing benchmark curves in Figures 6–12 are retained. New Figure 13 shows faster loss reduction for Cycle SGD in the added communication scenario. Figure 14 reports poorer convergence for B=512/1024 than B=128/256 under the displayed settings. These are additional findings, not improvements over v1 under unchanged settings.

T1.justification: Theorem 2.4's independence condition now includes the current iterates. Appendix D replaces a variance-decomposition step with Young's inequality, propagates factors of two, and corrects summation indices. New Appendix H derives a time-complexity comparison with canonical Local SGD/FedAvg, including an epsilon^-3/2 term in the comparison bound. These substantively revise the central proof and extend the theoretical analysis.

C1.justification: The abstract's framework, eight-method contribution, and optimality claims remain. Section 1.2 narrows coverage from 'virtually all' to 'a wide range' of distributed SGD methods and explicitly adds tighter time-complexity guarantees relative to canonical Local SGD/FedAvg as a contribution.

C2.justification: Beyond v1's homogeneous-data scope discussion, v3 identifies possible similarity assumptions needed for non-i.i.d. extensions and names preconditioning and non-Euclidean geometry as future extensions. Appendix I also makes the communication-family qualification of Dual-Process SGD's optimality more explicit.

D1.justification: The new experiments disclose selected learning rates and algorithm parameters in Figures 13–14, including Cycle SGD's group size. Existing hardware descriptions, Simpy setup, and Tables 2–6 remain unchanged. Neither version documents a code-release or access change.

R1.justification: New A.3 substantially expands positioning against other unifying SGD frameworks, including Cooperative SGD and the graph approaches of Even et al. and Huang et al., explaining differences in graph semantics and complexity measures. Appendix H adds a direct canonical FedAvg comparison using McMahan et al., Koloskova et al., and Luo et al.

P1.justification: v3 adds a Local SGD worked example and proof roadmap, splits Appendix D into explanation and proof, and places Insights and Guidelines before the experimental summary. Affiliations and acknowledgements also change. Most existing exposition and the overall organization remain recognizable.

P2.justification: Figure 4 expands from one computation tree into a three-stage construction illustration. v3 adds Figures 13–14 and Algorithm 20, boxes the main theorem, and adopts conference headers and styling. Existing benchmark plots and table structures are largely retained, with placement and numbering changes.

improvement.justification: The decisive gain is stronger theoretical reliability: v3 corrects the independence requirement and replaces v1's problematic variance-decomposition step with Young's inequality and consistent constants in the central proof supporting the framework. Appendix H and A.3 also address important gaps in comparison with canonical Local SGD and competing frameworks, while C.5–C.6 supply targeted empirical support. These gains substantially strengthen the paper despite remaining notation slips and the continued absence of empirical uncertainty reporting.
